summary: Inspect an ordered three-qubit GHZ state through its eight amplitudes, one- and two-qubit reductions and exact three-body Pauli parity settings.
objective: Inspect an ordered three-qubit GHZ state through its eight amplitudes, one- and two-qubit reductions and exact three-body Pauli parity settings.
intent_signals: Inspect GHZ correlations without replacing the joint state by Bloch arrows.
Compare the four XXX XYY YXY YYX parity settings for GHZ plus and minus.
example_prompts: Inspect GHZ correlations without replacing the joint state by Bloch arrows.
negative_signals: Claiming a hardware Bell test or faster-than-light signaling.
not_for: Claiming a hardware Bell test or faster-than-light signaling.
Encoding the eight-amplitude state by three local Bloch vectors.

entities.name: Eight-amplitude spine
entities.guidance: Use declared order |000> through |111>; show complex signs and normalization.

entities.name: Reduction deck
entities.guidance: Show three 2×2 single reductions and three 4×4 pair reductions separately.

entities.name: Parity stations
entities.guidance: Show X/Y setting per qubit, joint expectation and allowed outcome-product parity without generating hidden predetermined values.

state_contract.model: Accept one finite complex eight-amplitude pure state in declared |q_A q_B q_C> binary order, reject zero/nonfinite norm, normalize and form rho=|psi><psi|. GHZ+ is (|000>+|111>)/sqrt(2), GHZ- uses the minus sign. Compute all one- and two-qubit partial traces. For O in {XXX,XYY,YXY,YYX}, compute <psi|O|psi>. Exact GHZ+ has expectations (+1,-1,-1,-1); GHZ- has (-1,+1,+1,+1). Disable GHZ badges outside the exact-preset tolerance. Marginal states and correlators never replace the full joint state.
state_contract.authority: Supplied finite tensors, ordered identifiers, basis conventions and provenance own semantic state. Blender/glTF assets are display-only; Three.js owns validation, calculation, linked selection, failure states and exact reset.
actions: Select a one- or two-qubit reduction.
Select one Pauli setting and inspect amplitude pairing and parity.
Passively reorder qubits with complete index/operator/label permutation.
Reset state, order, setting and selection.

invariants: State and reduction traces equal one; all are Hermitian and PSD within tolerance.
For both exact presets each one-qubit reduction is I/2 and each pair reduction is (|00><00|+|11><11|)/2.
The four declared three-body expectations have the preset-specific signs and magnitude one within tolerance.
A passive tensor reorder preserves physics only when amplitudes, reductions, operator factors and labels permute together.
motion_guidance: Setting changes recompute an expectation from one frozen state; they do not animate measurement collapse, signaling or pre-existing outcomes.
creative_affordances: Choose any coherent laboratory, constellation or sculptural art direction while preserving exact labels, selectable identity and non-color encodings.
known_limits: Documentary authored recipe only; no model training, checkpoint execution, quantum hardware, Blender export, browser, renderer or interactive runtime was run.
glTF transports neutral display assets only; tensors, checkpoints, citations, basis order, dtype and provenance remain external data.

claims.statement: Mermin presents a three-spin GHZ state that is a simultaneous eigenstate of the three mixed X/Y Pauli products and has the opposite eigenvalue for XXX; the product constraints yield perfect three-body correlations.
claims.scope: Mermin’s GHZ-minus phase convention gives XYY, YXY and YYX eigenvalue +1 and XXX eigenvalue -1; the recipe derives the reversed signs for GHZ-plus explicitly.

source_refs.locator: Section III, equations (3)-(5), measurement-product discussion and Appendix state vector

object_craft.articulation: Three.js owns amplitude order, reductions, tensor operators, expectation arithmetic, complete passive reorder and reset.
